headline: SoftBank is reportedly weighing a purchase of Allied Universal, the largest US security services firm, in a deal worth up to about 30 billion dollars including debt, as founder Masayoshi Son eyes security work as a place to use robots.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: a possible multibillion-dollar deal tied to robots in the workplace, but it is early, unconfirmed talks.
importance_line: Security guards and the businesses and public bodies that hire them could see robots enter the work if a deal happens, but talks are preliminary and complex security jobs may stay hard to automate.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by Investing.com, that SoftBank Group is considering buying Allied Universal, which could be valued at up to 18 billion dollars in equity, or close to 30 billion dollars with about 12 billion dollars of publicly traded debt. Bloomberg says founder Masayoshi Son sees security as a promising field for robots, though talks are preliminary and no decision has been made.
notes: Same story as C11-05; the main session should keep one of the two. Original is Bloomberg (link above, behind a robot check); text read from the Investing.com copy on Yahoo Finance (finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/softbank-weighs-30-billion-allied-192903720.html).
